title: HULK Smash: Ramon's 177.86 Flattens Dawgs as Week 1 Rewrites the Title Odds
dek: No Banner only HULK posted the week's top score by more than 31 points, Randy's lineup hit 146, and Zoe won the first fantasy game of her career.
body: The 2026 season was one Sunday old when No Banner only HULK made the rest of the league look like it was still reading the rulebook. Ramon's team walked into Dawgs' building as a pregame underdog, with Mekhi given a 54% chance, and left with a 177.86 to 98.36 win. The 79.5-point margin was the largest of the week. Josh Allen scored 35.66 on a 19.32 projection, Kenneth Walker III added 32.6 on a 13.32 projection, and D'Andre Swift chipped in 31.9 on an 11.41 projection, giving the HULK three of the week's five best performances. The model noticed: Ramon's title odds rocketed from 11% to 47%, and his playoff odds already sit at 98%.

The most impressive detail might be what the HULK overcame. The Texans D/ST finished at minus 4 on a 5.25 projection, a defense that actively subtracted from the total, and the team still cleared 177. There is also something poetic about Brucie, the Chicago kid turned Bills fan, riding his Buffalo quarterback and a Bears running back to the top of the standings. On the other side, Mekhi got 2.2 points from Ja'Marr Chase on a 16.44 projection while Christian Watson scored 29.7 on his bench, a swing that would have made this loss merely bad instead of historic. Dawgs' title odds fell from 17% to 1%, the steepest drop in the league.

Randy delivered the week's other blowout, and his favorite team did most of the work. Caleb Williams scored 37.26 on a 16.39 projection, the best individual performance in the league, and Derrick Henry added 34.8 on a 15.72 projection as The fumblers beat Counting or not Counting GV 146.16 to 75.96. Not every Bear cooperated: Colston Loveland put up a zero on a 9.67 projection, so Randy got the full Chicago experience in one afternoon. The fumblers' title odds jumped from 15% to 28%, the second-best number in the league.

Jordan's opener was a lesson in how much one lineup decision can hurt, and in how sometimes it doesn't even matter. Ashton Jeanty scored 29.7 on his bench, the week's biggest bench blunder, and Counting or not Counting GV would have lost by more than 40 even with him in the lineup. The 75.96 was the lowest score of the week by more than 22 points. JMoney is here for the numbers, and the numbers are not being kind: 0% title odds and 3% playoff odds after one game.

Zoe's first game as a fantasy manager came against the league's two-time champion, and she won it. Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Habibsters 129.56 to 108.6 as a 48% home underdog, a 20.96-point margin that included a rookie-style bench miss: David Montgomery scored 27.4 while sitting. Z² still posted the third-highest score of the week, and her 13% title odds held steady while her playoff odds stand at 76%. Kaushal, meanwhile, watched his title odds collapse from 17% to 3%, and went to the wire to swap the Browns D/ST for the Jaguars D/ST, which is the fantasy equivalent of changing the locks after the house was already robbed.

The defending champ opened his title defense with the week's closest game. Sonny's The Horse is Hea beat Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1 as a 46% pregame underdog, winning by 4.32 despite Jahmyr Gibbs scoring 31.1 for Alan on a 20.48 projection. The model was unmoved by the result: Sonny's title odds actually fell from 9% to 4%, partly because his 106.4 points was lower than Kaushal's losing total. Sonny made the week's other move, adding Mark Andrews and dropping T.J. Hockenson at tight end, and Alan heads into Week 2 at 0-1 with 4% title odds after a game he could easily have won.

After one week, the league has already sorted itself into tiers. The HULK, The fumblers and Ghostu-Spider SZN hold a combined 88% of the title odds, and nobody else is above 4%. It is one game out of 14, which is plenty of time for a correction, but the gap between the top three and everyone else is already wide enough to see from space.

Week 2's headliner is No Banner only HULK against Ghostu-Spider SZN, a meeting of two unbeaten teams where Zoe gets to find out whether her opener was a fluke or a warning. Mekhi faces The fumblers and needs a response before a 0-2 start buries a 23% playoff outlook. Jordan gets Sonny in a game where Counting or not Counting GV's 3% playoff odds could use some company. And Team Pillbert hosts Habibsters, two 0-1 teams that were title contenders a week ago and now have to prove the model wrong.

social.text: 177.86. Allen, Walker, Swift all over 31. Our defense scored NEGATIVE FOUR and we still won by 79.5. Title odds 11% to 47%. Everybody else is playing for second.

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Dawgs were the 54% favorite. Ja'Marr Chase gave them 2.2. Christian Watson gave them 29.7 from the bench. That is not a loss, that is a cautionary tale.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Caleb 37.26. Henry 34.8. Loveland 0.00. We have experienced the full spectrum of Bears fandom in a single afternoon and we are 1-0.

social.author: Spider SZN Stans
social.text: Career record: 1-0. Beat a two-time champ by 20.96 with Montgomery's 27.4 on the bench. The rookie is not here to learn, she is here to collect.

social.author: The Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources: Habibsters responded to a 20.96-point loss by changing their D/ST. The offense has been informed it is next.

social.author: Bench Mob Report
social.text: Week 1 bench points left on the table: Jeanty 29.7, Watson 29.7, Montgomery 27.4. Two of those three teams lost. The third is very lucky to have a 129-point week.

social.author: Stat Line Sally
social.text: The Horse is Hea won and its title odds went from 9% to 4%. Sometimes the model watches your game and says no thank you.

social.author: Pillbert Partisans
social.text: Gibbs drops 31.1 and we lose by 4.32. Somewhere a 0-1 team is plotting revenge on Habibsters.
